label: Save
depicts: Floppy disk with one top notch window and one lower rectangular label area
use_when: Use when the interface wants the classic floppy disk metaphor instead of a document confirmation symbol.
avoid_when: Do not use for the checked page variant when the save state should read like a completed file rather than disk media.

label: Scan
depicts: Four open corner brackets forming one square scan frame with no center mark
use_when: Use when the interface wants a camera style scan frame built only from corner brackets.
avoid_when: Do not use for the circular scan variant when the mark should look like a ring with a sweeping diagonal segment.

label: Scan
depicts: Open circular ring with a diagonal sweep cutting across the upper right side
use_when: Use when the interface wants scanning to feel like a circular sweep instead of corner brackets around a frame.
avoid_when: Do not use for the corner frame scan when the mark should be four separated brackets with an empty center.

label: Scissors
depicts: Open scissors with two round finger loops below and crossing blades pointing upward
use_when: Use when the interface wants the familiar vertical scissors pose with loops at the bottom and blades above.
avoid_when: Do not use for the sideways or rotated scissors when the tool should not read as the standard upright cutting pose.

label: Scissors
depicts: Rotated scissors with one handle loop hanging lower left and one blade shooting upward past the crossing point
use_when: Use when the interface wants a more dynamic rotated scissors silhouette instead of the straight upright tool pose.
avoid_when: Do not use for the classic upright scissors or the sideways scissors where the cutting tool should face in a more stable orientation.
